evidence.claim: Scotland carries a name chosen by Isaac Magoon to commemorate his ancestral home.
evidence.quote: He named the town Scotland as a way of commemorating his ancestral home.

evidence.claim: He purchased 1,950 acres from Windham in 1700; Scotland became a separate town in May 1857.
evidence.quote: In 1700, Isaac Magoon purchased 1,950 acres (7.9 km2) of land from then Windham and thus began Scotland's History. He named the town Scotland as a way of commemorating his ancestral home. Scotland was incorporated in May 1857.

evidence.claim: The D’Elia Antique Tool Museum, established in the public library building in 2005, holds more than 1,200 antique woodworking planes, with examples dating to the middle of the eighteenth century.
evidence.quote: Scotland is home to the D'Elia Antique Tool Museum, a museum established in 2005 in the Scotland Public Library building. It holds more than 1,200 antique woodworking planes dating to the mid-18th century.

evidence.claim: Before the turnpikes, Rochambeau’s French troops used Scotland Road in 1781 on their way to Yorktown and again on their return in 1782, when they camped beside it.
evidence.quote: it formed part of the march route taken by French commander Rochambeau's French Army troops in 1781, on their way to Yorktown, Virginia, and also on the route of their return journey in 1782. On the return trip, the army established a camp in the field on the north side of this road section.
